assessments.evidence: Compared all 22 Overview and 21 Cloud installer Supported regions rows. The overview alone lists Dublin on 2024-06-28; all other region/date pairs are identical. AWS and four separate Azure SAIA service labels are present; Cloud hosting catalog is not the feature inventory. Both tables contain GovCloud East/West dated 2026-05-11 alongside commercial scope prose. October 19 announcement is limited to named SPL authoring and explanation in AWS GovCloud.

assessments.evidence: The 2.3.6 About section describes a separate regional AI service and same-region prompt processing when using a Splunk-hosted model. The installer retains separate activated-stack, subscription, public app installation and version conditions. Its full Supported regions table omits Dublin. Service-specific AWS/Azure names are mapped separately from Platform tenant hosting, identity and residency. Feature-specific routing can cross the selected geographic region.
assessments.qualification: Preserve AI service-location mappings and distinguish them from the tenant host or implied processing residency.

assessments.evidence: Cloud installer describes limited IL2 2.0+, Agent Mode exclusion, default-off training/fine-tuning and fixed Splunk-hosted runtime. October 19 announcement is for named SPL authoring and explanation in AWS GovCloud High. ES 8.8 Help GovCloud exceptions name Security AI Assistant and Agentic SOC. Observability Assistant excludes GovCloud, from its own official Availability evidence. No implied Moderate/High runtime, ES/ITSI component authorization or tenant eligibility.
assessments.qualification: Separate the documented feature-level regulated boundary from offering authorization. Preserve exclusions and unknowns.

assessments.evidence: The Agent Mode feature guide gives an independent AWS supported-region list including Dublin and Enterprise 10.1.x+ floor, Model Runtime activation and Agent Mode toggle. The Model Runtime table separately lists AWS Dublin from v2.3.0 with Global routing and supplies per-region Data zone, Global or Azure N/A classifications. A Global entry may route across regions. Azure Model Runtime rows and the Agent Mode list do not settle baseline SPL or ITSI availability.
assessments.qualification: Agent Mode and Model Runtime have their own region evidence; derive no feature inheritance from the base assistant.

assessments.evidence: The 2.3.6 feature guide describes a Cloud Connected 2.1+ path with eligible region, enablement, Model Runtime, bidirectional network access and trusted certificate requirements. The 2.3.6 installer and dated SAIA-9918 issue row exclude 2.2.0 through 2.3.6 from Cloud Connected installation and give 2.1.1 fallback without Agent Mode. The separately published 2.4.0 release and installer require Enterprise 10.4+, Cloud Connect 2.0+, paid license and fresh certificate/permission/activation setup. That separate installation path does not clear Agent Mode prerequisites, region, runtime processing or tenant enablement.
assessments.qualification: Cloud Connected Agent Mode regional/runtime availability and compatibility stay independently scoped.

assessments.evidence: 2.3.6 About ITSI subagent requires ITSI 5.0.0+, MCP Server 1.2.1+ and SAIA 2.2.0+. No separate ITSI Dublin rollout appears in that feature section. The regional rows and installation guides are for the base assistant; neither independently establishes this subagent. Keep the exact dependency thresholds and its regional uncertainty together.
assessments.qualification: Keep ITSI-specific regional enablement unresolved where a public scoped source does not establish it.

issueObservations.rationale: FR2314156865 remains FedRAMP Certified Class D and its public package certified_services list is empty. The dated vendor matrix remains separate from current Marketplace data and from customer eligibility.

F1607197917 remains FedRAMP Certified Class C and its public package certified_services list is empty. The same-day High read has its own separate result. An empty public field leaves named service scope unresolved.

The 10.7 Victoria table gives AWS Israel and the change log limits its addition to the relevant scope. The two public reports show the current Israel evidence separately from historical release availability.

The Yes/No experience matrix and regulated endpoints prose still disagree for High Victoria. The maintenance guide excludes High operations and the tested reader asks for operation-specific confirmation.

The 10.7 S3 row excludes High and IL5 but includes Moderate. Broader third-party federation restrictions separately exclude Moderate, High and IL5. Preserve distinctions, including the separate 10.3 change-log evidence cited in the review.
The service description maps us2 to Google Cloud Oregon (us-west1). Its US Database Monitoring row still lists us2 and None in the Google Cloud column.

Full 2.3.6 tables differ only on Dublin, which the About page lists and the installer omits. Both live Dublin reports and exports preserve the difference and the separate Agent Mode listing. The source discrepancy remains open.
The ITSI, MCP Server and SAIA floor versions appear in About. The independent Dublin rollout remains undocumented, and that qualification was present on both public reports and exports.

Dublin is Global in the Model Runtime entry from 2.3.0. The feature guide requires enabled Model Runtime for Agent Mode. The separate Cloud Connected assurance does not settle feature-specific routing beyond a selected region.

The known issue excludes Cloud Connected for 2.2.0–2.3.6 and its 2.1.1 fallback lacks Agent Mode. The released 2.4.0 installer documents a fresh supported Cloud Connect installation, independent of Agent Mode prerequisites and tenant activation.

The October announcement covers named core SPL functions, and the 2.3.6 documented IL2 path fixes the model runtime and excludes Agent Mode. Current 2.4.0 release notes separately mark core SPL support with no Agent Mode in supported High environments. Exact region, version-specific runtime policy and tenant rollout still need confirmation.

The current Essentials and Premier tables preserve the named Calgary/GovCloud exclusions and do not apply a blanket Security AI Assistant exclusion to Milan or São Paulo. Montréal has a named Cloud Connect exception and Calgary does not. The verified Cloud Connect reader displays the Montréal exception.
The Assistant Availability page still lists us3. The service-description realm-to-region table still does not map that realm. The commercial Virginia reader refers to its own documented mapping.
The aggregate 8.8 Cloud entry still gives ES 8.6+ and detailed Cloud task evidence still specifies ES 8.7+. Named CMP prerequisites are separate.
The current aggregate has a Cloud-only Response availability column alongside CMP prerequisite text. The task remains Controlled Availability and does not qualify unlisted deployments.
The parent task retains 200 daily analyses and the 20-revision example. The linked Triage task retains a first-ten findings note and a warning about reruns. Exact work-item limits remain qualified.

Both former ES 8.8 source URLs again returned 404. The exact renamed vendor offerings and setup topics were retrieved and their applicable passages assessed. The old registered historical locators remain visible.
The detailed 8.8 Autonomous Response task prohibits reruns and later-added findings and requires frontier models. Triage revisions do not clear those scope limits.
